subject: AI & Agents
title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
description: A short lesson to help you apply Chain-of-Thought Reasoning.

hook.text: Ask an LLM a math problem directly: wrong. Ask it to show its work: correct. Why?

buildup.text: Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to reason through intermediate steps.

discovery.text: By generating step-by-step reasoning, the model avoids shortcuts that lead to errors.

twist.text: The model isn't actually 'thinking.' It generates tokens that look like reasoning, and they help.

climax.text: This technique improves accuracy on math, logic, and multi-step problems dramatically.

punchline.text: Even AI works better when it shows its work.

quiz.question: Why does chain-of-thought prompting improve accuracy?
options: Step-by-step reasoning helps the model avoid shortcuts
It makes the model run faster
It accesses a different part of the model

details.summary: Chain-of-thought prompting asks LLMs to show their reasoning step by step before giving an answer. This simple technique dramatically improves accuracy on math, logic, and complex reasoning tasks.
details.whyItMatters: Chain-of-thought revealed that LLMs can reason more carefully when asked to. It changed how people interact with AI and inspired reasoning models that think step-by-step automatically.
takeaways: Asking LLMs to reason step by step improves their accuracy
It works especially well for math, logic, and multi-step problems
It inspired dedicated reasoning models like OpenAI's o1

faq.question: Why does chain-of-thought work?
faq.answer: LLMs generate each token based on previous tokens. When forced to spell out intermediate steps, each step conditions the next, reducing errors. Without explicit steps, the model must jump directly to answers.

faq.question: When should you use chain-of-thought prompting?
faq.answer: For math problems, logical reasoning, code debugging, multi-step analysis, and any task requiring sequential thought. For simple factual questions or creative tasks, it adds unnecessary overhead.
